To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nurses’ judgments about the classification of patient care errors are not consistent and that their judgments about risk associated with these errors are not consistent.
nurses’ ability to classify and rank the severity of patient care errors is suboptimal.
nurses' judgments of the classification and risk of patient care errors are less than optimal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how nurses make judgments about errors and their associated risk in clinical practice.

how nurses working in a variety of clinical settings can improve their ability as front line clinicians to recognize subtle cues in the clinical situation to facilitate early recognition and reporting of potential errors.
the role of nurses in patient safety and their potential to contribute to patient safety improvement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

nurses are not good at classifying and risk level of patient care errors, but that this is not surprising given that the classification and risk level of errors in health care are not well understood.
the results of this study suggest that registered nurses' judgments of the classification and severity risk of patient care errors are not optimal.
nurses are not always in agreement on the severity or risk level of a given error and that more research is needed to better understand how to improve this process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ability to recognize and respond to errors in real time is an important aspect of patient safety and that nurses are in a unique position to improve their ability to do this.
nurses are not always good at recognizing errors, but they are very good at recognizing the potential for errors.
nurses need to be more aware of the potential for patient harm and to develop skills to recognize and mitigate the impact of adverse events.
The main takeaway from our work is that

nurses need to improve their ability to classify patient safety events, which can be accomplished by improving the accuracy and reliability of the event classification system used by the Joint Commission and others.
there are opportunities to enhance nurses' abilities to recognize and respond to potential errors in patient care, which can help to reduce harm.
nurses need to be trained in error recognition and management, and this training needs to include a focus on the cognitive processes that lead to errors and their mitigation.
